question.worked_solution:
The multiplicative inverse of $9$ modulo $11,$ denoted ${9}^{-1},$ is the number $x$ such that

$$
9\cdot x≡1\,(\text{mod}\,11).
$$

Note that since $\text{gcd}(9,11)=1,$ an inverse element exists and is unique up to congruence modulo $11.$

Since the modulus $n=11$ is small, we can find the inverse $x$ by computing exponents of $9$ (modulo $11$) until we get a result of $1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{9}^{2} & ≡9\cdot 9≡81≡7\cdot 11+4≡4 &  & (\text{mod}\,11) \\ {9}^{3} & ≡9\cdot 4≡36≡3\cdot 11+3≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,11) \\ {9}^{4} & ≡9\cdot 3≡27≡2\cdot 11+5≡5 &  & (\text{mod}\,11) \\ {9}^{5} & ≡9\cdot 5≡45≡4\cdot 11+1≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,11)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $9\cdot 5≡1\,(\text{mod}\,11).$ Therefore, the multiplicative inverse of $9$ modulo $11$ is $5.$
